messages:
mira: Heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak in canary, we're seeing 90th percentile host-side tokenization jitter on HTTP/gRPC paths. Not pure model decode, looks like preparse + reactor scheduling.
jon: ugh. timeline? did the change land to all canaries or just one pool?
priya: just pool-3 canary. changed kernel chooser to prefer fast-matmul variant for seq<=64 (fallback for long seqs).
mira: exact. regression shows up as frequent 2–8ms spikes per request before we hand off to the runtime. baseline used to be ~1ms for preproc.
sam: can you paste the perf flame? also which path — hosted API ingress or dedicated proxy?
mira: hosted ingress (grproxy). flame: perf sampled while replaying a burst of small requests.
perf-bot: link: https://perf.internal/redwood/flames/1719504000-canary-token-jitter
mira: relevant snippet from flame: lots of time in grpc::Server::OnRead + tokenize::ByteSpan::normalize -> then syscall wait on epoll. Looks like the gRPC reactor is getting rescheduled mid-tokenize.
jon: makes me think tokenization is happening on the IO thread. Are we doing tokenize on grpc cq thread instead of dispatch pool?
priya: yes, we pushed a micro-opt to do tokenization inline to reduce copies. That reduced median earlier but now it blocks cq -> scheduling jitter under burst.
sam: proposal: revert inline tokenize and move to short-lived preflight worker queue (bounded) so cq stays responsive. Also add fast-path for ascii-only tokens to avoid allocations.
mira: experiments: queueing to preflight pool removes the 2–8ms outliers but adds a steady 0.5ms handoff; net 90th improves. But KV cache hit rate dropped 3% because preflight ordering changed (different batching heuristic).
priya: ah the batcher keying is sequence-length-first; moving to preflight disturbs arrival ordering -> kvcache sees more unique prefix hashes -> evictions.
jon: can we keep original ordering for kvcache lookups before preflight? i.e., quick peek for KV key on cq thread (cheap non-blocking) then hand off tokenization.
sam: that could work if we keep peek super cheap. Maybe peek only first 32 bytes -> compute prefix hash.
mira: ran microbench: prefix-peek (32b) adds 0.15ms on cq but avoids kvcache miss surge, and 90th is now ~1.2ms. flame looks clean.
priya: another angle: kernel selection policy may encourage smaller batches (seq<=64) which increases per-request overhead at host. If we instead tier by throughput hint we can coalesce more on host-side batching.
jon: right — if kernel selection is too eager to use low-latency matmul, it prevents grouping similar sequences into a single GPU batch. Need a cross-layer signal from batcher to kernel selector.
sam: action item: add a 'batchable' hint to kernel selector. If requests arrive within 5ms window, prefer larger-kernel path even if slightly heavier for single-request latency.
mira: quick triage timeline: PR to revert inline-tokenize -> preflight-queue + prefix-peek (mira) — immediate. PR for batchable hint (priya+jon) as next. Also add canary that measures kv-hit and 90/99 pctl for hosted. Sam own canary rollout.
priya: I'll open the batchable-hint RFC today. I'll include the perf numbers and a simple simulation showing GPU batch size vs per-host overhead.
jon: I'll help wire the peek kvcache check into grproxy. Sam, can you own the canary dashboard (add kv-hit, 90/99 host-preproc)?
sam: on it — will add alert if kv-hit drops >1.5% or 99th host preproc >15ms.
mira: thanks. leaving this thread with owners. TL;DR: inline-tokenize caused cq-reschedule spikes; moving to bounded preflight + cheap kvcache-peek fixes most regressions; batcher/kernel coupling needs longer term work. :thumbsup:
